paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub awesome. It is time for GitHub trending weekly number 30. We have tracked down 35 trending repositories on GitHub. Let's get into it.

3dsvg turns any 2D SVG into an interactive 3D component in your browser. Drag in an SVG. Pick from 10 material presets like glass, chrome, or holographic. Add animations like floating or spinning. And export as a 4K transparent PNG or 60fps MP4 using FFmpeg Wasm running entirely locally. Hit embed and get a clean React JSX snippet using React Three Fiber ready to drop straight into your Next.js project. AI coding agents write great code but terrible visual documentation. Markdown Viewer skills is a collection of 15

Installable AI skills that teach your agent to use seven different rendering engines. Mermaid, PlantUML, draw.io, Graphviz, and more. Enterprise cloud architectures, UI wireframes, dependency trees, even floor plans generated directly inside your markdown files. Quien bundles WHOIS DNS records, mail server info, SSL/TLS certificate details and HTTP header detection into a

Single beautiful TUI. ARDA lookups first graceful voice fallback. Run subcommands like quien DNS or quien stack and get perfectly structured JSON. Install it as a Claude Code skill and your agents can run programmatic domain investigations without writing a single regex parser.

Fireworks tech graph is a Claude Code skill that generates technical architecture diagrams from plain English. Type draw a multi-agent collaboration diagram with an orchestrator and three sub-agents in glass morphism style and it renders a professional-grade visual straight into your workspace preloaded with structural knowledge for RAG pipelines, memory setups, agentic search and tool calling architectures.

iOS marketing capture is a Claude Code skill that builds an automated screenshot system directly into your SwiftUI project. So it has zero footprint in production. Trigger it and it seeds your app with demo data and loops through all your supported locales by relaunching under different language environments. Even captures isolated SwiftUI elements like widgets with perfect transparency using ImageRenderer.

Y Combinator CEO Gary Tan open sourced his personal AI knowledge system. Gbrain is long-term memory for AI agents. Everything you know, people, companies, deals, meetings, stored as markdown files in a git repo. While you sleep, it scans your conversations, emails, meeting transcripts, enriches entities, creates cross-references, builds a knowledge graph. You wake up. Your digital brain got smarter overnight.

Bouncer is a browser extension that filters social media feeds by phrases, topics, or emojis, removing matching posts without breaking the scroll. The bounce this post button is the clever part. Click it on any post that annoys you. A local AI analyzes it and suggests three reasons why. Pick one and similar posts disappear permanently. The filter gets smarter every time you use it.

AI debuggers guess at fixes from static code and sometimes break something else in the process. Debug agent changes the approach entirely. Install it as a Claude Code or Cursor skill. Run debug agent and instead of guessing, the AI injects lightweight NDJSON logging and asks you to reproduce the bug. It analyzes live runtime logs to confirm or reject hypotheses, only writes a fix when it has actual evidence, then verifies automatically.

If you run the Hermes AI agent, you need to see what it's actually thinking. Hermes HUD brings a full consciousness monitor to your web browser. It reads directly from your agent's local data directory, giving you real-time visibility into memory vaults, active sessions, and loaded skills. Per-model token cost tracking so you can see exactly how much your autonomous agent is spending in real time.

Switching from Windows to macOS means leaving 7-Zip behind and nothing on Mac has properly filled that gap. ShichiZip is a native macOS 7zip derivative built entirely in Swift and Objective-C++. No Electron wrapper, no generic cross-platform UI, full seven-zip format support, plus a custom Zstandard fork variant for modern fast compression running natively on Apple silicon.

Quip node manager is a cross-platform desktop GUI built on Rust and Tauri v2 that gives you a clean visual interface to configure, run and monitor your nodes. Native or Docker works on macOS, Linux and Windows out of the box. Handles config, TOML files, secrets, binaries, and your trust database automatically. No cloud telemetry, no SaaS pipeline, just a window into your agent's actual state.

AI agents hallucinating facts from complex documents is a trust problem that breaks legal, financial, and academic workflows. Liteparse fixes the verification layer. Point your agent at a folder of documents and it generates a structured HTML report where every extracted fact includes an interactive link that opens the source document and draws a bounding box around the exact text on the page.

Most terminal spinner libraries for Rust are bloated or require complex runtime integration. Rattles takes a compile-time first approach. All animation data, braille patterns, emoji, and ASCII presets baked directly into your binary at compile time. No runtime, no life cycle management, no dependencies. Works in no_std environments out of the box. Drop it straight into your Ratatui render loop at zero cost.

Tired of massive bloated Python frameworks just to build an AI agent? Helixent is a lightweight TypeScript library built on bun for constructing React-style agent loops. Reasoning, planning, executing, the core cognitive loop of autonomous agents with none of the orchestration bloat. Raw minimal building blocks for custom agent loops, LLM tool execution and CLI skills at maximum speed.

You merge a simple refactoring PR, publish the new version, and suddenly your GitHub issues are full of people saying you broke their code. Tsnapi fixes that by bringing snapshot testing to your public API contract. Every build generates two human-readable snapshot files, a snapshot.js for runtime exports and a snapshot.d.ts for TypeScript declarations.

Local Azure development means juggling Azurite, the Cosmos DB emulator, functions core tools, and more. Miniblue replaces all of it with a single Docker command. 21 different Azure services running locally on one port. Blob storage, key vault, Cosmos DB, Azure Functions. All of it works with your existing Azure SDKs, Terraform, and Pulumi setups. No Azure account, no network connection, no credit card.

Managing multiple Claude Code sessions across tmux panes means constantly hunting for which agent needs attention. Tmux-agent-sidebar adds a real-time sidebar that tracks the active status, prompts, git drift, and activity logs of every agent across all your tmux. See which repos are active, which agents are waiting for input, and press enter to jump directly to any agent's pane.

File Converter Pro is a fully offline Windows desktop app. Documents, images, audio, video, all from one tool. Your files never leave your machine. Multi-engine fallback so every conversion works. Auto-detects Microsoft Office, LibreOffice, FFmpeg for higher quality output. Statistics dashboard, gamified achievements, rank-up celebrations, confetti particles, seasonal overlays.

Karpathy's argument: RAG is broken because it just retrieves the same raw chunks every time. His fix: let an LLM autonomously write and maintain a persistent markdown knowledge base. LLM Wiki is the open source implementation. Upload your PDFs, connect Claude via MCP, and it synthesizes encyclopedia-style articles, flags contradictions, and updates cross-references across dozens of files simultaneously.

Most approaches feed raw SVG tokens straight into a language model. HiVG compresses them hierarchically instead. Raw commands fold into atomic tokens. Atomic tokens fold into learned segment tokens. 2.76 times shorter than what competitors feed their models. 3 billion parameters. Beats GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 on image to SVG conversion. Give it a PNG. Get back an editable SVG. Give it a text prompt. Same deal.

Most Obsidian AI plugins let you chat with your notes. This one writes them. Drop a source, an article, a PDF, a GitHub repo, and Claude reads it, extracts entities and concepts, cross-references everything already in your vault, and files it. No manual tagging, no folder decisions, and an eight-category vault linter that catches orphan pages and dead links before they pile up. AI coding agents build functional UIs.

They rarely build beautiful ones. StyleSeed fixes that with 69 strict visual design rules, 48 components, and 11 installable AI skills. Shadows at 4% opacity, balanced typography ratios. Pick a skin inspired by Stripe, Linear, or Vercel. Copy the engine files into your project. Your agent generates production-ready interfaces that actually look intentional.

Standard image libraries crash Cloudflare workers. The memory limits are just too tight. SIP is a memory-efficient image processing library built specifically for those constraints. Resize, process, and optimize images with a microscopic memory footprint directly on the edge. No bouncing payloads back to a heavy AWS backend just to crop a photo. Prep images for your AI vision agents right where the request lands.

Swift MTP is a native macOS utility built entirely in SwiftUI. Uses the Colom backend from OpenMTP under the hood but strips away all the web app bloat. Plug in your Android phone, it detects it automatically and you get a Finder-style interface with drag and drop in both directions. Handles files over 4 GB without freezing. Remotion lets you build videos in React.

What it doesn't ship with is a component library. So every fade, wipe, and kinetic title gets written from scratch. Remocn is a shadcn-style registry that fixes that. Blur reveals, chromatic aberration wipes, a terminal simulator, a browser flow scene, a full product launch trailer composition, all tuned and ready to edit. A fully functional VS Code instance in a single 25 megabyte npm package with zero dependencies.

Coderaft packs the entire VS Code editor into a platform-agnostic package you can run on any machine and access straight from your browser. Spin up remote dev environments or embed an enterprise-grade code editor into your web app with almost zero overhead.

Giving an AI agent raw terminal access is a genuine security risk. Boxsh is a sandboxed POSIX shell built on Dash designed specifically to be driven by AI via a concurrent JSON Lines RPC protocol. Linux namespace isolation traps every command in a secure sandbox so your agent can run builds, install packages, and execute scripts without touching your host machine. Most hardware monitoring tools are locked to one OS or one GPU vendor. HBM works across NVIDIA,

AMD, and Intel GPUs on both Windows and Linux. It reads telemetry directly from low-level vendor APIs and renders core temperatures, power draw, clock frequencies, PCIe traffic, and VRAM bandwidth in a retro ASCII visualization right in your terminal.

AI agents are great at JavaScript, but terrible at raw terminal commands. They hallucinate flags and crash your environment. Cli-to-js fixes that by reading the help output of any binary on your system and converting it into a fully typed JavaScript API. Subcommands become functions. Flags become object properties. Your agent calls structured JS instead of piecing together fragile shell strings.

Mesurer is a lightweight measurement and alignment overlay for React apps. Toggle it with a keyboard shortcut. Click elements to see exact bounding boxes. Drop vertical and horizontal guides onto your page and hold Alt to reveal pixel distances between components instantly. Full undo/redo history and state persistence so your guides survive a page refresh.

NotebookLM will turn your docs into a podcast. You can't touch the script, the hosts, or the voices. This project gives you all of that. Pointed at a URL, a PDF, a meeting transcript. Claude writes a two-host conversation script. Fish Audio generates the speech. FFmpeg stitches it into an MP3. Feed it your own writing, your resume, your browser history, and ask the host to analyze you as if you're not in the room.

Recreating Apple's progressive blur headers in SwiftUI is notoriously painful. Harsh cutoffs, hard clipping, gradient mask hacks. ProgressiveBlurHeader solves it in one line of code. As content scrolls under your header, it smoothly blurs with a flawless gradient, exactly like Apple Music, Photos, and the App Store. Uses a private Apple API under the hood to bypass standard SwiftUI limitations.

CleanMyMac costs a yearly subscription, tracks your usage, and constantly upsells you. Pure Mac is the open-source alternative. MIT licensed, runs entirely offline, zero analytics, clears system junk, Xcode derived data, Homebrew caches, and APFS Time Machine snapshots. Click to inspect shows exactly what gets deleted before you commit. Background automation automates the whole thing.

Most AI memory systems rely on massive vector databases and expensive embedding models. Hypatia takes a completely different approach named after the scholar of the library of Alexandria. It's a lightweight memory system built entirely in Rust. SQLite FTS5 and DuckDB tied together with a custom JSON query language. No external models, no fuzzy vector embeddings.

SciWrite is a single skill file built on the entire methodology from Dr. Kristen Sanani's writing in the sciences course at Stanford compressed into a machine-actionable format. Drop it into your workspace and your AI becomes a scientific editor. It flags passive voice, eliminates academic jargon, and explains exactly why a sentence is clunky based on the Stanford methodology.
